due_when.clears_when: BOTH halves, and they are separate: (a) THE BINDING -- the sweep fires somewhere it can actually run: an unattended session (the route the E44 cold test proved survives a cold container) or create_new_session_on_fire=true. [!] PRICE IT ON A MEASUREMENT THAT DOES NOT EXIST YET. The only cold-firing figure on record is ~$7.40 against ~$0.15 warm, and the E44 lane CORRECTED its own headline on 2026-09-23: that firing ALSO hit the main-vs-branch mandate defect and then went off-mandate opening a PR, so it is an UPPER BOUND ON A MIS-WIRED FIRING, not a steady-state price. A firing that stops at step 1 as designed should cost far less and NOBODY HAS MEASURED ONE. Do not quote ~$7.40 as the per-firing cost; measure a clean firing first, then choose. (b) THE OBSERVABILITY -- a firing produces an artifact that is ABSENT when the firing did not run. scripts/ci/check_manager_queue_watch.py ALREADY grades exactly this for a sibling watcher and currently reports NEVER_RAN_OVERDUE at ~508 expected firings with ZERO receipts, so the receipt mechanism is half-built and unwired rather than missing. Fixing (a) alone leaves the next silent failure just as invisible. [!] WHAT DOES NOT CLEAR IT: last_run reading SUCCEEDED (it read SUCCEEDED for all 25 firings that supervised nothing), a manager promising to check, or this manager having drained the queue by hand once on 2026-09-23.

Then ask whether THAT session is attended -- a human-driven session is the defective binding; an unattended one is fine and is the proven route. A SUCCEEDED last_run tells you nothing either way. what: THE HOURLY LANE-SWEEP BACKSTOP SUPERVISED NOTHING FOR 24 HOURS BECAUSE IT IS BOUND TO AN INTERACTIVE SESSION. The Routine `Manager lane sweep -- hourly backstop behind the report-back wire` (trig_01L2skxWuvPCPiQHMWooDPAj) fires into session_01XQhayAHWdrSYv8jN54P2HH -- a session a human drives from the Claude app. MEASURED 2026-09-23T18:52Z by draining that session's notification queue: 25 firings between 2026-09-22T18:43Z and 2026-09-23T18:43Z, and EVERY ONE QUEUED AS A NOTIFICATION rather than running. A firing into an ATTENDED session waits behind the human; it does not take a turn on its own. Its `last_run` reads SUCCEEDED for all 25, because that field grades DELIVERY. [!] WHAT THIS IS NOT, and the first draft of this row got it wrong in the expensive direction. It is NOT `persistent_session_id Routines do not run`. That claim is FALSIFIED by primary evidence read from git, not from a session's report: commit eeb416937 on `claude/e44-lane-supervisor-build` carries `Claude-Session: session_01R9WFrBK1sbBcpTYgBmvG1q` and was pushed 2026-09-23T18:46Z after that session had been idle for hours -- a cron firing woke an UNATTENDED session, which then ran tools, wrote a file and pushed. The E44 lane's cold-test receipt (trig_01QQEz7pdn5uyyxrZ6QyiWYg, 2026-09-22T18:29:43Z) reports the same route surviving a COLD container (worker_epoch 2 -> 3) with checkout and mcp__* tools intact. ATTENDED-QUEUES and ROUTE-DOES-NOT-RUN ARE OPPOSITE DIAGNOSES AND ONLY THE COLD TEST SEPARATES THEM. A lane reading the first draft would have ripped out a mechanism that had just been proven. So the route works; THE BINDING IS THE DEFECT. [!] WHAT IT COST, measured over exactly that 24h window: the one live lane (E44, session_01VsAt1BzrdspLn6hDzFTGh2) went from inside its $60.00 ceiling to $207.47 (3.5x) with no ceiling read, and E30's lane (session_017mdYduTwtyVPXU54wqNHJx) sat walled on a permission prompt for 29 hours with nobody surfacing it. Those are precisely the two failures sweep items 6 and WALLED exist to catch. [!] THE DURABLE PART: a delivered-but-unrun firing is INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A CLEAN SWEEP in every view there is. list_triggers shows last_run SUCCEEDED; nothing anywhere records that no sweep output was ever produced. That is the same `we could not look` vs `we looked and found nothing` collapse CLAUDE.md names as a bug class, sitting on the supervision mechanism itself.
